- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/27 (Mon) 10:15
- [USER] User asked about the evolution of the relationship between Indonesia and the Philippines.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The relationship between Indonesia and the Philippines has gone through various ups and downs over time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Initially, both countries had a good relationship due to shared experiences under colonialism and struggles for independence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The relationship was strengthened when both countries became members of ASEAN in 1967.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the mid-2000s, a maritime border dispute emerged over the Mindanao Sea, leading to tensions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Philippine government filed a formal protest against Indonesia's continuation of oil exploration within the disputed area.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In recent years, the relationship has improved as both countries worked towards resolving territorial disputes peacefully.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Indonesia and the Philippines have strengthened partnerships in trade, tourism, education, and culture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both countries cooperate on regional initiatives such as the Coral Triangle Initiative.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Coral Triangle Initiative aims to preserve and protect marine biodiversity and promote sustainable economic growth in Southeast Asia.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The relationship has evolved from cooperation and mutual understanding to tensions over territorial disputes, and now towards renewed cooperation.
- [USER] User asked about the steps taken by the governments of Indonesia and the Philippines to resolve their maritime border dispute.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The maritime border dispute involves a small area in the Mindanao Sea claimed by both countries as part of their exclusive economic zones (EEZs).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Indonesia and the Philippines have engaged in bilateral negotiations facilitated by the Joint Technical Working Group (JTWG) on Maritime and Ocean Concerns, established in 2015.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The JTWG has recommended the formation of a joint boundary committee to settle the dispute.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 2017, both countries agreed to conduct joint patrols in the disputed area to prevent illegal fishing and maritime crimes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both countries submitted claims to the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) to settle the dispute.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 2018, Indonesia and the Philippines agreed to settle the maritime border dispute through arbitration under the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) in The Hague.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both governments are committed to resolving the dispute through peaceful means and continue to engage in dialogue and negotiations.
